title: Tool adapter multiplexer: reconcile OpenAI-style tools with legacy function contracts
creator: Leila Park
description: We need a runtime-level adapter that can accept incoming tool invocation requests in either OpenAI-style tool descriptors or our legacy function contract format and reliably route them to the correct execution surface. The goal is to enable single API surfaces, preserve streaming semantics, and minimize breaking changes for existing customers while enabling new OpenAI-compatible integrations. This ticket defines the multiplexer approach, edge cases for naming collisions, structured output normalization, and a migration plan.
background: Customers are adopting both OpenAI-style tool schemas and our legacy function-based integrations. Current attempts to support both in the runtime are ad-hoc, leading to duplicate mapping logic, missed streaming hooks, and inconsistent error semantics. We observed incorrect routing when tools were aliased differently across integrations and inconsistent provenance metadata in audit logs.
proposed_solution:
Introduce a 3-layer adapter multiplexer deployed in the serving runtime: 
1) Canonical registry: at startup, the multiplexer builds a canonical name map from model-usable tool names to runtime function endpoints. It supports explicit aliases and scoped namespaces (customer/model/route).
2) Signature reconciler: a translation layer that coerces incoming params (OpenAI-style JSON schema) into the legacy typed function payloads and vice versa, preserving validation errors and field-level provenance. Use a lightweight, pluggable coercion library with schema hints to avoid hard-coding transformations.
3) Streaming-aware dispatcher: the final step routes calls while preserving streaming token frames for compatible backends, and falls back to buffered responses for legacy backends that do not support streaming. Implement a per-call policy: prefer streaming when both sides support it, otherwise use passthrough buffering with a streaming envelope to the client.
Additional features: structured-output normalizer to canonicalize JSON/typed outputs; conflict resolution rules for duplicate tool names (prefer explicit aliasing, then per-namespace match, then fallback to deterministic tie-breaker); detailed invocation provenance logged per-request (original name, resolved canonical name, translation hints, fallback reasons).
acceptance_criteria: Adapter multiplexer implemented in runtime-1.20 branch and deployable behind a feature flag.
Registry supports per-tenant aliases and resolves duplicate names deterministically with documented tie-break rules.

Signature reconciler can translate at least the 6 most common param type patterns (primitive coercion, arrays, objects, optional fields, enums, file/bytes placeholders) and surfaces validation errors in client-friendly form.

Streaming dispatcher preserves token-level streaming when backend supports it; when backend does not support streaming, client sees streaming envelope with 'streaming_fallback' event and then final payload.
Structured-output normalizer produces stable JSON Schema-conformant outputs for tool calls and a test harness evaluates 100 sample tool calls to verify round-trip fidelity >= 98%.
End-to-end integration tests cover OpenAI-style request -> adapter -> legacy function backend and legacy request -> adapter -> OpenAI-compatible backend.
Documentation: runtime docs page + migration guide for customers and an example SDK snippet for registering aliases.
No high-severity performance regressions (p50 latency change < 5%) for tool-invocation paths in benchmark suite.
Audit logs include invocation provenance fields for every adapted call.
notes: We intend to keep the adapter light: no deep semantic rewriting (e.g., no NLP-based name guessing). For ambiguous cases operators can register explicit mappings via Console or infra config. The feature flag should allow routing all adapted calls through a shadow path for 2 weeks before flipping.
